verified.fact: James II arrived Ireland March 1689; Derry and Enniskillen were substantial local Williamite opposition, Williamite multi-national forces
Derry sustained siege and relief in summer 1689, National Army Museum says August; avoid invented single relief date for now
Boyne 1 July 1690 Old Style; modern July 12 commemoration is not same as contemporary date; armies Williamite 36000 Jacobite 25000 per Irish Office of Public Works
James's army withdrew in order; military defeat Boyne did not end war and should not be dated to end in 1690
Aughrim 12 July 1691 in NAM Gregorian dating; reports of more than 7000 killed not independently audited, refrain exact deaths
3 October 1691 civil and military articles are two distinct sets; religious and estate safeguards have eligibility conditions and promise to seek additional legislative protection

Clarke account reports words 'and all such as are under their protection in those counties' omitted from final clean copy article 2; later relief cannot be interpreted as automatic application to every Irish Catholic
Military articles give soldiers and eligible family members leave to embark overseas except England and Scotland; evidence does not give all who actually departed in 1691
Confiscation and postwar land rights cannot be quantified as modern Ireland shapefile or universal forfeiture; Irish government archival index refers to confiscated-land hay/harvest proclamations
